steps.say: NEC is the commonest surgical emergency of the newborn gut, and prematurity is driving almost every case. Ischemia, bacterial overgrowth, cytokines and feeds are injuring the immature bowel together. Gradual breast milk based feeds are lowering the incidence on modern units.
steps.tx: **Necrotising enterocolitis** (preterm gut injury) is the most common gastrointestinal surgical emergency in neonates, driven by ischemia, bacterial overgrowth, cytokines and feeds, with **prematurity** (early birth) as the dominant risk. **Breast milk** (human milk) based gradual feeds lower the incidence on modern units.

steps.say: A preterm baby who was feeding well and then balloons with bloody stools is showing NEC until proven otherwise. Distention, tenderness, cellulitis, bloody stools and feeding intolerance cluster with temperature instability, apnea and bradycardia. Eighty percent strike in the first month, with feeds started in the first days.
steps.tx: Hallmarks are **abdominal distention** (swollen tense belly), tenderness, cellulitis, **bloody stools** (blood in nappies) and **feeding intolerance** (residuals and vomiting) with temperature instability, apnea and bradycardia. **80** percent strike in the first month, with feeds begun in the first days of life.

steps.say: Gas inside the bowel wall itself is the signature finding, and it is visible on a plain film. Pneumatosis intestinalis from bacterial hydrogen is pathognomonic, with portal venous gas, fixed loops, ascites and free air as companions. Disease usually hits the distal ileum and ascending colon first.
steps.tx: **Pneumatosis intestinalis** (gas cysts in bowel wall) from bacterial hydrogen is pathognomonic, with **portal venous gas** (liver branch air), fixed loops, ascites and **free air** (perforation leak) as companions, usually hitting distal ileum and ascending colon on plain films. Films may also show separated loops with thickened walls before gas appears.

vis.alt: Bowel cutaway showing submucosal and subserosal gas cysts with giant cell histology beside CT with intramural gas and portal venous gas.
vis.caption: Pneumatosis from bacterial hydrogen is pathognomonic, with portal venous gas and free air as companions. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: More than half of affected babies recover without an operation, provided watching is genuinely continuous. Over half the cases are resolving with medical management using tube decompression, fluids and broad spectrum antibiotics. The team stays at the bedside watching for surgical triggers around the clock.
steps.tx: Over half the cases resolve with **medical management** (nonoperative care) using tube **decompression** (stomach venting), fluids and **broad spectrum antibiotics** (wide germ cover) under close watch. **50** percent and more settle medically, but the threshold for exploration stays low throughout.

nodes.label: Tube decompression, fluids and broad antibiotics
Over half resolve; watch for triggers

steps.say: Free air under the diaphragm is ending the debate and booking the theatre at once. Free air (pneumoperitoneum) is the absolute surgical indication for exploration. Deterioration, acidosis, cellulitis, a palpable mass, fixed loop and portal gas are relative triggers that are pushing most surgeons to operate.
steps.tx: Free air (**pneumoperitoneum**, leaked intestinal gas) is the absolute **surgical indication** (mandate to operate), while **clinical deterioration** (worsening despite maximal care), acidosis, cellulitis, palpable mass, fixed loop and portal gas are relative indications for exploration. Tachycardia with falling platelets strengthens the decision to explore promptly.

vis.alt: Abdominal cutaway showing purulent peritonitis with bowel edema beside axial section and open abdomen decompressive laparotomy.
vis.caption: Peritonitis with free air mandates exploration; deterioration and fixed loops lower the threshold. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The operation is saving length first and finishing the job later, because short bowel is crippling the survivor. Principles are resecting dead bowel, saving length, and diverting with an ostomy or damage control discontinuity. Ischemic but viable segments get a second look at 24 to 48 hours before final decisions.
steps.tx: Principles are **bowel resection** (removing dead segments), saving length, and diverting with an **ostomy** (stoma) or **damage control** (discontinuity) approach. Second look follows at **24** to **48** hours for merely ischemic segments, and primary anastomosis suits only rare focal perforations.

rows: Damage control, second look 24 to 48 hours

steps.say: Tiny babies tolerate drainage under local anaesthetic when laparotomy feels too much. Bedside peritoneal drainage matches laparotomy for survival, parenteral need and stay in infants under 1500 grams in a multicentre randomised trial. Drainage is sometimes proving definitive without further surgery.
steps.tx: Bedside **peritoneal drainage** (abdominal drain) matches laparotomy for survival, parenteral need and stay in **extremely low birth weight** (under **1500** g) infants in a multicentre **randomised trial** (Moss et al NEJM 2006), and drainage sometimes proves definitive alone. Ventilated infants tolerate the drain insertion with local anaesthetic and sedation.

steps.say: Survivors need watching for narrowings, and the splenic flexure is the classic site. Strictures are complicating 10 percent after any management, typically at the splenic flexure, so contrast enema precedes stoma reversal. Surgically managed disease carries 10 to 50 percent mortality plus neurodevelopmental delay.
steps.tx: **Stricture** (healed narrowing) complicates **10** percent after any management, typically at the **splenic flexure** (left colon bend), so contrast enema precedes stoma reversal. Surgically managed disease carries **10** to **50** percent **mortality** (death rate) plus neurodevelopmental delay in survivors. Growth and development clinics follow survivors for feeding and learning progress.
